conservation.technical_description:
Surface: The surface has intermittent small accretions and fibrous debris throughout. There are a few hairline cracks ranging from about 1/2" to 1 1/2" in length along the far outer edges of the surface at the upper center, upper right and lower left. The surface has a couple areas very minor loss at the upper right in the blue sky portion. There is a series of intermittent abrasions running along the far outer edge at the upper left of the surface. 
 
Frame: The frame shows signs of wear throughout with minor cracks and scratches, loss of gilding, minor nicks, abrasions and accretions. At the upper right corner is a single long 6 3/8" horizontal crack that continues inward towards the center of the frame.

credit_line: Collection of the New Mexico Museum of Art. Gift of the Georgia O’Keeffe Estate, 1987 (1987.312.3)
description: The gray and brown limbs of a tree rise from the earth. Masses of green foliage cling to the tree. Drifts of cloud-like cottonwood seeds, in the form of hazy gray shapes, emerge from the tree. Bits of blue sky and red hills are visible in the scene's background.
